note: Proposals are not source revisions. Any actual change must edit both meaning formulation and supporting paraphrase observation appropriately, use an approved exact-predecessor revision, invalidate/review dependent graph links, and re-screen changed content. Do not apply in Phase 2.

proposals.old: Let R→S be a finite-type ring homomorphism and q∈Spec(S) lying over p∈Spec(R). The map is quasi-finite at q if q is an isolated point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)); equivalently its local fibre has dimension zero.
proposals.suggested: Let R→S be a finite-type ring homomorphism and q∈Spec(S) lie over p∈Spec(R). The map is quasi-finite at q if q is an isolated point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)); equivalently, q is closed in this fibre and the local ring of the fibre at q has Krull dimension zero.
proposals.reason: q=(0) in Spec(k[t]) has local fibre ring k(t) of dimension zero but is not an isolated or closed fibre point. For a finite-type algebra over a field, the fibre is Noetherian and Jacobson, so closedness plus zero local dimension yields the finite isolated component condition.

proposals.old: A continuous map f:X→Y is submersive if it is surjective and Y has the quotient topology for f; equivalently, U⊆Y is open exactly when f^{-1}(U) is open in X.
proposals.suggested: A continuous map f:X→Y is submersive if and only if it is surjective and, for every subset U⊆Y, U is open in Y exactly when f⁻¹(U) is open in X.
proposals.reason: For a non-surjective map from a singleton into a discrete two-point space, all subsets satisfy the open-preimage biconditional but f is not onto.

proposals.old: A topological ring is a ring R with a topology for which its addition R×R→R and multiplication R×R→R are continuous maps.
proposals.suggested: A topological ring is a ring R with a topology making its additive group (R,+) a topological group (both addition and additive inverse are continuous), and making multiplication R×R→R continuous.
proposals.reason: Under a nonunital ring convention, zero multiplication on Z with the upper-set Alexandrov topology has continuous addition and multiplication but discontinuous negation.

proposals.old: Given a topological ring R, a topological R-module is an R-module M endowed with a topology such that addition M×M→M and scalar multiplication R×M→M are continuous.
proposals.suggested: Given a topological ring R, a topological R-module is an R-module M whose additive group is a topological group and whose scalar action R×M→M is continuous.
proposals.reason: For a potentially nonunital module action, R=Z and M=Z with upper-set topologies and zero action satisfy continuous addition/action but fail additive-inverse continuity. Ring unity alone does not fix a zero module action.

proposals.old: The perfect closure of a field k of positive characteristic p is its smallest perfect extension obtained by adjoining all compatible p-power roots of elements of k inside a fixed algebraic closure.
proposals.suggested: For characteristic p>0 retain the stored p-power-root construction. Add a separately attributed characteristic-zero convention k^perf=k, because every characteristic-zero field is perfect; retain the existing scoped formulation as a valid special case.
proposals.reason: Two geometric normality/reducedness formulations invoke k^perf without specifying p>0; the stored perfect-closure construction itself explicitly assumes p>0, and should not be falsely tagged mathematically wrong.

proposals.old: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of finite free modules, its rank is the largest integer r for which the induced exterior-power map ∧^rφ is nonzero (and is zero when φ itself is zero).
proposals.suggested: Define rank(φ)=0 when φ=0; otherwise define rank(φ)=max{r≥1 : ∧^r φ is nonzero}. State that the zero-map convention takes precedence over the maximum clause, including R=0.
proposals.reason: When R=0 the zeroth exterior-power map is itself zero, so the set of nonzero exterior powers is empty; a separate zero-map rule preserves the zero ring without adding R≠0.
